python_environment: OpenAI analysis runtime; Python 3.x, numpy, scipy 1.17.0
matched_budget_unit: player-level marginal observations; one iid permutation yields five marginal observations

adaptive_estimator.name: minimax player/coalition-size stratification with time-uniform alpha-spending Clopper-Pearson intervals
adaptive_estimator.warm_start: one uniformly sampled marginal from each of 25 player/coalition-size strata
adaptive_estimator.allocation: choose player with widest mean stratum interval; within that player choose widest stratum; deterministic-seed random tie breaks; sample coalition uniformly with replacement
adaptive_estimator.confidence: for stratum sample count m, alpha_m = 0.05 * 6 / (pi^2 * 25 * m^2); two-sided Clopper-Pearson; union bound over 25 strata and all positive m

interpretation: The uncertainty-directed allocator improves aggregate RMSE at moderate/high matched observation budgets, but its point estimate misses the rare nonzero bridge more often than iid permutation sampling. At 320 observations the adaptive bridge-zero rate is 25.9% versus 9.6%; at 640 it is 10.1% versus 1.4%.
Therefore optimizing average attribution error or allocating only to currently wide aggregate intervals is not a safe lemma-elimination objective when rare but real interactions matter.

The time-uniform alpha-spending confidence sequence is safe but far too conservative for practical demotion: even at 640 observations the median upper bound for the true 1/30 bridge credit is about 0.642 and the median widest player interval is about 0.643.
Point estimate zero and safe evidence of zero are distinct. A zero point estimate cannot authorize demotion while its valid upper interval remains large.

For this five-player game, exact evaluation is preferred: there are only 2^5 = 32 coalition utility values, so Monte Carlo attribution is unnecessary. This fixture is a warning for larger candidate universes, not evidence that this adaptive allocator should be deployed.
design_update: Keep an explicit exploration floor / rare-effect guard in any large-universe adaptive estimator.
Do not choose stopping/elimination solely by aggregate RMSE or point estimates.

Use estimator-specific uncertainty with materially tighter anytime guarantees than naive alpha-spending Clopper-Pearson, or exploit finite-population exact/without-replacement structure when feasible.
All coalition attribution remains advisory for library promotion/demotion unless chronologically future fixed-compute causal utility confirms value.
